chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Hassan from Ibn Abi Imran from Abdullah ibn al-Hakam said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who testified against a man that he pushed a boy into a well and he died. He said: 'Upon the man is one-quarter of the boy's blood money by the testimony of the woman.'
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for a boy killed by a man according to the testimony of one woman?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a woman's testimony is sufficient to establish liability for one-quarter of the child's *diyah* (blood money), rather than requiring two women to match one man. This ruling highlights the specific application of testimony ratios in financial compensation (*diyah*) within Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from general civil cases where two women are typically required for one man. It underscores the precision of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in deriving legal consequences directly from the evidentiary weight of a single female witness.
